Yes. I would put **“end-to-end” immediately under the main headline** because that is the simplest way to explain why you are different from a typical marketing agency.

### Replace the current subheader with:

**We’re an end-to-end growth agency built exclusively for med spas and aesthetic practices. We don’t just get you leads. We build the entire system that turns them into booked appointments, repeat clients, members, and referral machines.**

Then directly underneath:

**We diagnose your market first** so we know exactly who to target, what they want, and what type of ads will actually work in your area.

Then our **aesthetics-only marketing team** turns on the acquisition faucet and brings in better-fit leads.

But unlike most marketing agencies, **we don’t hand you a list of leads and disappear.** We follow up, nurture, and book those leads directly onto your calendar.

And we don’t stop once they show up. Our proprietary retention system and **15 proven playbooks** help turn one-time appointments into repeat clients, members, and referral machines.

**Because the goal isn’t just to get you another $600 Botox appointment. It’s to help turn that client into a $6,000+ lifetime relationship.**

### Or, even punchier at the very top:

**WE’RE THE END-TO-END GROWTH AGENCY FOR MED SPAS.**

**We diagnose your market. We attract better leads. We book them directly onto your calendar. Then we help turn them into lifetime clients.**

**From first click to repeat visit, membership, and referral, we help you build the entire system that turns marketing into long-term revenue.**

That is much clearer than the current **“You need an aesthetics growth partner who understands…”** language. fileciteturn0file0 The visitor should understand within about **five seconds**: *Oh, they don't just run my ads. They handle the entire journey from acquiring the lead to helping me keep the client.*

Yes. The current copy under the header is **too vague**. It says you “understand how to turn better leads into booked, paying, returning patients,” but it does not clearly explain **how** or why TLC is different. fileciteturn0file0

I would replace the current subheader and the **“Most marketing agencies focus on getting you leads and stop there. We don’t.”** section with this:

### Recommended version

**We don’t stop at getting you leads. We build the entire system that turns them into long-term, high-value clients.**

First, we **diagnose your market** to understand exactly what your ideal clients want and what will make your practice stand out.

Then, our **aesthetics-only marketing team** turns on the acquisition faucet with strategic ads designed to attract better-fit leads.

But we don’t hand you a spreadsheet of names and disappear. We **follow up, nurture, and book those leads directly onto your calendar.**

And once they become clients, our proprietary retention system and **15 proven playbooks** help you turn one-time appointments into **members, repeat clients, and referral machines.**

**The goal isn’t just to get you a $600 Botox appointment. It’s to help turn that client into a $6,000+ lifetime relationship.**

### If you want it even shorter and punchier for the very top of the page:

**We don’t just get you leads. We turn them into booked appointments, repeat clients, members, and referral machines.**

We diagnose your market, run your ads, follow up with every lead, book qualified prospects directly onto your calendar, and help your team turn one-time appointments into long-term, high-value clients using our proprietary retention system and 15 proven growth playbooks.

**Because the goal isn’t another $600 Botox appointment. It’s turning that client into a $6,000+ lifetime relationship.**

I think the **second version is stronger for the landing page hero**. It immediately tells the med spa owner exactly what you do without making them work to understand it. Then farther down the page, you can visually break the process into:

**DIAGNOSE → ATTRACT → BOOK → RETAIN → GROW**

That would make the entire offer much clearer than the current long paragraph on page 2.
